requirements: docs/34 Verified workflow economics and routing observability
scenarios: an initial leg on the economical solver fails (NO_PROGRESS): the request record says fail, initial leg false, with the compiler's decision (every candidate's mean/LCB) and every plan version, pinned by RequestOutcomeRecorded at the run's end

an operator plan prevalidates the stronger solver; the resumed run escalates and succeeds: request pass and verified, not first-pass, initial leg still false, escalation success true, path CASCADE, the gate's REJECT kept with NONE_OBSERVED
every attempt reconciles token for token (input, cached subset, output, provider request id) with the scripted provider's reported usage, and the cost equals those tokens at the registry's prices
a person's ACCEPT is an explicit signal by reference with a REVIEW_DECIDED record; a restarted Core rebuilds the same record

a provider answer without usage and an invocation a Core kill cut off hold their slot's reservation; a late invoice settles one once at the registry's prices; a duplicate charges nothing; wrong request id, missing attempt, bad subsets, a reported attempt and a client without provider.configure are refused
unit: tenant filtering, replayed attempt dedupe, a retention-removed payload listed unavailable, per-subset pricing

ci.note: every Rust job green on macOS, Linux and Windows; the macOS desktop-E2E job passed on rerun after the documented CAPACITY_EXHAUSTED timing flake

audit: IMPLEMENTED-PARTIAL before: plans, admissions, activations, attempts (input/output, unknown kept unknown), continuations, reviewer legs, gate evaluations were on the log, but nothing assembled a request's accounting: no cached subset, latency or price per attempt, candidates' mean/LCB dropped, reviewer-task usage unlinked, cut-off invocations untraced, no settlement, no late-invoice path, no request/leg/gate attribution, no raw-signal record; the Messages adapter's input_tokens excluded cache reads.
proof: On the real Core against a scripted OpenAI-compatible provider over HTTP, an escalated request's record reconciles to the provider's own usage report and keeps request, leg and gate observations apart; a kill, a missing usage frame and a late invoice are accounted without loss or double charge.
negative_proof: Before the change the escalated request had no record at all; the Messages adapter reported 50 input tokens for a 50 plain + 40 cached message billed as 90; the FI refusals and the duplicate delivery are the negative cases of the invoice path.
limitations: Retention deletion exercised at the accounting boundary (payload object removed), no product retention operation yet (docs/31 Retention owner); verification time reported, not priced; keep signal and composite reward named missing (no keep window, no reward version); model calls outside routing attempts (compaction, vision bridge) are not request attempts yet; live-provider half rides any live run.
